coverage.statement: This site publishes who is officially unavailable. It does not publish who replaces them, because no official source read in this session names a replacement. Inventing one would corrupt the very signals the deficiency feature is meant to produce.

slot_model.rule: A depth slot is a group of players at one rank, not a single starter. A slot may hold several players and may be empty.
slot_model.why: Several position slots across the league list more than one player at rank 1 - three receivers, three inside linebackers. Treating column 1 as 'the starter' fabricates a starter the club never named.
slot_model.shared_slot: Two or more players listed at the same rank for the same slot. Stored as a list; the render shows both and flags the slot as shared. It must never be silently reduced to one name.
slot_model.empty_slot: A slot the club publishes with no player in it. Stored with an explicit flag, so an empty slot is distinguishable from a slot we failed to capture.
slot_model.raw_string: The published string is stored verbatim next to the parsed fields, so a parser change can be replayed against the original text. This is what recovers clubs whose pages prepend jersey numbers.

rejections.rejected: Deriving depth order from jersey number
rejections.reason: Jersey number correlates with nothing that determines who plays. It would produce a confident, wrong ordering on every club that renumbered a free-agent signing.
Experience is a proxy for past availability, not for the club's current intent. Rookies start; veterans sit.
Salary is a proxy for past negotiation, not for this week's game plan, and it is wrong in the direction that matters most when a cheap replacement has already taken the job.

rejections.rejected: Inferring a replacement from the injury report
rejections.reason: The official report has no replacement field. Any name attached to an absence would be a guess presented as a fact.

rejections.rejected: Transcribing a depth chart published as an image by eye
rejections.reason: It is unverifiable and unreplayable. The requirement names the correct fix: an authorised structured source, not transcription.

known_parse_failures.proposed_fix: Number stripping does not help. Requires an authorised structured source.

known_parse_failures.failure: Jersey numbers prepended to player names
known_parse_failures.proposed_fix: Number stripping plus storing the raw string recovers the rows.
known_parse_failures.status: fix specified, not applied - no parser exists yet

snap_count_proxy.rule: Where a club's depth chart is unavailable, snap counts are the starter proxy - playing time, not jersey order.
snap_count_proxy.why_threshold_is_null: The threshold defines the label. Setting it after seeing who it labels is fitting the definition to the answer. It must be set before the first transcription (Q-DEPTH-02).
snap_count_proxy.source_note: Official Game Book PDFs are published per game on the official game centre; 12 of the 14 week 10 fixtures publish one. None has been parsed.

deficiency_matrix.purpose: One screen showing offense vs defense mismatches by string: a WR1 against a promoted 2nd or 3rd string cornerback, or an EDGE1 against a 2nd or 3rd string tackle or guard.
deficiency_matrix.cell_contents: The matchup, the string on each side, and a link to the dated source for each side
deficiency_matrix.status: Grid published and empty. Every cell requires a verified depth source (Q-DEPTH-01). It ships empty on purpose: an empty grid states the cost of the depth gap, and a filled-by-inference grid would hide it.
deficiency_matrix.why_shipped_empty: Requirement R-52 says resolve the depth-order source before building the backup-deficiency feature. The grid is the feature's shape, published early so the gap is visible, not the feature itself.

per_team_view.purpose: Quick team-level decision view: starters out, replacements named, net injury count.

columns.note: Count of rows with game status Out. Doubtful is counted separately, not folded in.

columns.reason: Requires a verified depth source to know who is a starter (Q-DEPTH-01)
The official report has no replacement field
Net against what baseline? Without a reserve list and a depth source the denominator is unknown, so publishing a net number would invent one

staleness_check.rule: Flag any depth row that is older than the last official roster event affecting that club's unit.
staleness_check.why_it_matters: Roster turnover redefines depth for weeks. A depth row that predates a trade or an injured-reserve move is worse than no row, because it looks current.

announced_starter_field.rule: An announced-starter field records a link to an official dated announcement of a starter change. It is never filled by inference and never used to imply a replacement.
announced_starter_field.note: This is deliberately a different field from 'replacement'. A club announcing a new starting quarterback is an official fact; who that pushes to second string is not published and is not inferred.
